prerequisites: Basic knowledge of computer network security problems at the level of popular trade magazines (e.g. c't)

learning_outcomes.text: Students will have a comprehensive understanding of the technical aspects of network security.
Students will have recognized that cryptography alone is not sufficient to solve security problems.
Students will have acquired a comprehensive system understanding for complex IT systems.
Students will prepare for their role in professional life through independent considerations for improving network security.
Students can analyze new problems and develop new solutions.
Students can argumentatively justify the utility of the solutions they have developed in conversation.
Students will have understood that non-technical factors such as liability and resulting costs significantly influence IT security decisions.

syllabus_topics: GSM and UMTS mobile communication (authentication and encryption)
IPSec (ESP and AH, IKEv1 and v2, attacks on IPSec)
File encryption with OpenPGP (data format, Efail, Klima-Rosa)
Email encryption with S/MIME (SMTP, data format, Efail, POP3, IMAP)
Published attacks on these systems will also be discussed
Students will undertake scientific considerations for improving security
assessment_rules: Credits are awarded upon passing the exam. The exam is a 120-minute written examination.
